1. An apparatus suitable for optical coherence tomography, OCT, scanning comprising:means for providing a first signal;
means for providing a reference signal;
a photonics integrated circuit comprising (i) means for receiving a reflected first signal, reflected from a subject;
(ii) means for coupling the reflected first signal to the reference signal to provide an interference signal, and
(iii) a variable delay for varying an optical path length of one of the reference signal and the first signal to match the optical path length of the reference signal to an optical path length of the reflected first signal, wherein the variable delay comprises at least one binary switch for selecting between paths of different lengths; and means for analyzing the interference signal.
2. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the variable delay comprises a series of binary switches and path elements of different selectable lengths.
3. The apparatus of claim 2, wherein the path elements are of length L, 2L, etc. up to 2NL,
where N is an integer.
4. The apparatus of claim 3, wherein the variable delay is a binary delay implementing a delay,SVG {EMBED HERE} 0.1570.217
in steps of L, of 0 to (2x2NL.
5. The apparatus of claim 2, 3 or 4, wherein the variable delay has N delay path elements and
N+1 binary switches, one binary switch before each delay path element, to selectively switch between a direct path or the delay path element, and one binary switch at the output to selectively switch from the direct path or the final delay path element to an output of the variable delay.
6. The apparatus of any one of claims 2 to 5, wherein the switches are two-way multiplexing or
demultiplexing switches.
7. The apparatus of any one of the preceding claims, wherein the variable delay acts on the reference signal.
8. The apparatus of any one of the preceding claims, wherein one of the paths of different lengths includes a tunable labyrinth with integrated phase shifter.
9. The apparatus of any one claims 1 to 8, wherein the means for providing the first signal is a broadband light source and the means for analyzing the interference signal is a spectrometer.
10. The apparatus of claim 9, wherein the spectrometer is implemented as one of an arrayed waveguide grating, AWG, a ring bus, a ring fan-out, a binary asymmetric Mach-Zehnder interferometer, AMZI, or an AMZI fan out.
11. The apparatus of any one of claims 1 to 8, wherein the means for providing the first signal is a swept laser source and the means for analyzing the interference signal is a point photodetector.
12. The apparatus of any one of the preceding claims, wherein the means for providing the reference signal is a beam-splitter, wherein the beam-splitter beam-splits the first signal.
13. The apparatus of any one of the preceding claims, wherein the means for coupling is a 2 x 2 coupler, wherein the 2 x 2 coupler is one of a directional coupler, a multimode interferometer or a Mach-Zender interferometer.
14. The apparatus of any one of the preceding claims, wherein the photonic integrated circuit comprises a first path for guiding the first signal to a set of imaging optics to the subject and for guiding reflected light from the subject back from through the set of imaging optics to the means for coupling and a second path for guiding the reference signal to a reflector and back to the means for coupling.
15. The apparatus of claim 14, wherein the first and second paths comprise polarization- maintaining fibres for maintaining polarization of the first signal and the reference signal
respectively.
16. The apparatus of any one of the preceding claims, wherein the means for remote viewing of the analyzed interference signal is an output image processor and the means for remote control of the variable delay is an on-chip control unit.
17. A method suitable for performing an optical coherence tomography, OCT, scan comprising:providing a first signal provided by a light source;
providing a reference signal;
reflecting the first signal from a subject and coupling the reflected first signal to the reference signal to provide an interference signal;
adjusting a delay of one of the reference signal and the first signal by a variable delay to match an optical path length of the reference signal to an optical path length of the reflected first signal, wherein the step of adjusting comprises selecting between paths of different
lengths; andanalyzing the interference signal.
18. The method of claim 17, comprising automatically selecting between the paths of different lengths until an interference peak is identified in the interference signal.
19. The method of claim 18, comprising performing image recognition on the interference signal to identify the interference peak.
